questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, one-time gstack onboarding before the PLAN.md design review.
ELI10: gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules, so plain requests like "review this diff" or "why is this failing" route to the matching skill automatically instead of you typing the slash command. This is a one-time prompt per project. Plan mode is active, so if you say yes the CLAUDE.md edit and commit happen after plan mode exits, not now.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without routing you invoke every skill by hand; with routing you get automatic skill dispatch you may not have wanted.
Recommendation: A because routing rules make the skill suite discoverable with zero ongoing cost.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: automatic skill dispatch vs. fully manual invocation.

ELI10: gstack records small lessons after each session (project quirks, pitfalls). questions.question:
D3 — Issue 1: How should Save be distinguished from Reset, Cancel, and Export?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, PLAN.md design review, Pass 1 Information Architecture.
ELI10: The header shows four buttons that look exactly alike. Users scan, they do not read, so the first glance has nothing that says "this is the one you want". Someone who just edited their email may hover between Save, Reset, and Cancel and pick wrong, which on Reset or Cancel means a confirmation dialog they did not want. DESIGN.md already says Save is the only filled primary button and the other three are neutral ghost buttons.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Users hesitate at the moment of commitment, or hit Reset/Cancel by mistake; the page reads as assembled rather than designed.
Recommendation: 1A because DESIGN.md already prescribes the exact treatment and it makes Save the one visual anchor on the page (Principle 2: every screen has a hierarchy).
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=7/10, 1C=3/10
Net: exact design-system conformance vs. a three-tier hierarchy DESIGN.md does not define vs. leaving the gap open.

options.label: 1A: Save filled primary, others ghost (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Save is the only filled #1d4ed8 button with white text; Reset, Cancel, Export are neutral ghost buttons, exactly per DESIGN.md
✅ One visual anchor; DOM/tab order and 44px targets unchanged, so no accessibility retest beyond contrast (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
❌ Export loses visual weight even though some users come to the page just to download

options.label: 1B: Save primary, Export outlined secondary, Reset/Cancel ghost
options.description:
✅ Three tiers: commit, download, destructive-ish, giving Export a bit more presence
✅ Save is still the single filled anchor
❌ Adds an outlined button style DESIGN.md does not define, so it is a new token decision (human: ~2h / CC: ~10min)

options.label: 1C: Leave all four buttons identical
options.description:
✅ Zero styling work; nothing new to verify
✅ Keeps the current look users have already seen
❌ Ships the documented violation; no primary action; litmus check 2 stays failed

questions.question:
D4 — Issue 5: What does the user see while Save is pending for 2-5 seconds?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, PLAN.md design review, Pass 2 Interaction States.
ELI10: After clicking Save, nothing changes on screen for up to five seconds. People assume the click did not register, click again, or leave. The plan already disables repeat submissions, but a disabled button with no other change just looks broken. DESIGN.md already defines the pending pattern: a small spinner beside the word "Saving…" inside the disabled Save button, aria-busy=true, and a non-animated fallback for reduced-motion users. Export already uses this exact pattern.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Users lose trust at the exact moment they commit their data; screen reader users get no pending announcement.
Recommendation: 5A because it is the established pattern Export already uses and it keeps the user's edited fields fully visible (Principle 9: trust is earned at the pixel level).
Completeness: 5A=10/10, 5B=6/10, 5C=5/10
Net: reuse the existing pending pattern vs. text-only feedback vs. hiding the form behind a skeleton.

options.label: 5A: Spinner + “Saving…” inside disabled Save (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Exact DESIGN.md pattern, already implemented for Export, so it is reuse not new work (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
✅ aria-busy=true plus the visible label change gives sighted and screen reader users the same signal; reduced-motion users get a static indicator
❌ Spinner lives only in the button; a user scrolled down to Notifications may not see it

options.label: 5B: InlineStatus text “Saving…” only, no spinner
options.description:
✅ The live region announces the pending state wherever the user is on the page
✅ No animation at all, so reduced-motion is trivially satisfied
❌ Deviates from the DESIGN.md pending pattern and leaves the Save button itself looking merely disabled (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)

options.label: 5C: Full-form skeleton or overlay while saving
options.description:
✅ Impossible to miss; also blocks edits during the atomic save
✅ Reuses the existing loading skeleton component
❌ Hides the values the user just typed, feels like a page reload, and is not the DESIGN.md pattern (human: ~3h / CC: ~15min)

questions.question:
D5 — Issue 4: What type scale should form labels and section headings use?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, PLAN.md design review, Pass 4 AI Slop Risk (flat-type-hierarchy).
ELI10: Labels on the form are set in three different sizes (14, 16, 18px) with no rule behind which gets which. Three sizes doing one job reads as noise, and the 14px ones fall below the 16px body-text floor that keeps text readable for everyone. DESIGN.md defines exactly two roles: 16px for body, labels, and helper text, 20px for the Profile and Notifications headings.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Small labels stay hard to read on phones; the page keeps the "assembled, not designed" feel; a future engineer inherits an undefined scale.
Recommendation: 4A because two roles are what DESIGN.md prescribes and they give a real hierarchy: headings clearly above everything else, everything else equal (Principle 3: specificity over vibes).
Completeness: 4A=10/10, 4B=5/10, 4C=3/10
Net: the design-system scale vs. a documented three-size scale that keeps sub-16px text vs. leaving it undefined.

options.label: 4A: 16px labels/body/helper, 20px section headings (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Exactly the two DESIGN.md type roles; nothing on the form drops below 16px (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
✅ Headings become the only larger text, so scanning by headline works and litmus check 3 stays YES
❌ Helper text at the same size as labels loses a subtle secondary cue; weight or color must carry it

options.label: 4B: Keep three sizes but define roles (14 helper, 16 label, 18 heading)
options.description:
✅ Codifies what exists today, so minimal visual change for returning users
✅ Gives helper text a distinct size cue
❌ Contradicts DESIGN.md and keeps 14px text below the 16px readability floor (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)

options.label: 4C: Leave label sizes as they are
options.description:
✅ No styling work now
✅ Nothing to re-verify visually
❌ Ships the documented violation with an undefined scale and sub-16px labels

questions.question:
D6 — Issue 2: What vertical spacing rhythm should the form use?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, PLAN.md design review, Pass 5 Design System Alignment.
ELI10: Gaps between sections are 24px in one place, 32px in another, and 16px in a third. Spacing is how users know what belongs together (Gestalt proximity): a bigger gap says "new section", a smaller gap says "this label belongs to this input". Random gaps blur that grouping, so the eye cannot tell where Profile ends and Notifications begins. DESIGN.md defines an 8px base: 32px between sections, 24px between field groups, 8px from a label to its input.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Grouping stays ambiguous; the form reads as unfinished; each new field gets its own guessed margin.
Recommendation: 2A because DESIGN.md already defines the scale and three distinct steps encode the three levels of grouping the form actually has (Principle 2: hierarchy; Gestalt proximity).
Completeness: 2A=10/10, 2B=6/10, 2C=3/10
Net: the three-step design-system scale vs. one flat gap everywhere vs. leaving it inconsistent.

options.label: 2A: 8px base: sections 32, field groups 24, label-to-input 8 (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Exactly the DESIGN.md scale; every gap on the form maps to one of three named values (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
✅ Section, field, and label grouping each get a distinct step, so proximity does the work without borders or cards
❌ Requires auditing every existing margin on the form, including the header action group and InlineStatus

options.label: 2B: Uniform 24px between everything
options.description:
✅ Simplest possible rule; one value to remember and verify
✅ Still consistent, so the random-gap problem disappears
❌ Flattens section vs. field grouping (monotonous-spacing) and contradicts the DESIGN.md scale (human: ~30min / CC: ~3min)

options.label: 2C: Leave spacing as it is
options.description:
✅ No layout work now
✅ No risk of shifting content users are used to
❌ Ships the documented violation; grouping stays ambiguous

questions.question:
D7 — Issue 3: How should the error message meet WCAG AA contrast?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, PLAN.md design review, Pass 6 Responsive & Accessibility.
ELI10: The error message is red text on light pink at about 3:1 contrast. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for text this size, so people with low vision or a dim phone screen may not be able to read the one message that tells them why their save failed. DESIGN.md defines the tokens: text #991b1b on surface #fef2f2 (about 7.6:1, passes AA and AAA) with an icon and explicit wording, so the state never depends on color alone.
Stakes if we pick wrong: The failure message is unreadable for the users most likely to need it; the page fails an accessibility audit.
Recommendation: 3A because the DESIGN.md pair clears AA with room to spare and the icon plus text satisfy the never-color-alone rule (Principle 7: accessibility is not optional).
Completeness: 3A=10/10, 3B=6/10, 3C=3/10
Net: the design-system error tokens vs. an ad hoc darker red on the current pink vs. leaving it below AA.

options.label: 3A: #991b1b text on #fef2f2 surface, icon + explicit text (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Exactly the DESIGN.md error tokens; measured contrast about 7.6:1, clearing AA (4.5:1) and AAA (7:1) (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
✅ Icon plus explicit wording means the state is readable without color, for colorblind users and screen readers alike
❌ Every existing error surface (field errors, ErrorSummary, inline retry area) must be re-checked against the new pair

options.label: 3B: Darken the red on the current pink until it measures 4.5:1
options.description:
✅ Smallest visual change from what users see today
✅ Meets the AA floor once measured
❌ Introduces a color pair DESIGN.md does not define and leaves the icon/explicit-text rule unaddressed (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)

options.label: 3C: Leave the error styling as it is
options.description:
✅ No styling work now
✅ Nothing to re-measure
❌ Ships a known WCAG AA failure on the most important message on the page

questions.question:
D9 — Deferred debt TODO: replace the app-wide system-ui font with a chosen typeface?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-XQbt40 on main, PLAN.md design review, post-pass TODO proposal.
ELI10: The form inherits the app's font, system-ui, which means "whatever the operating system uses". The design checklist treats that as the "gave up on typography" signal because the product has no typographic voice of its own. This plan correctly keeps it: swapping fonts on one settings page would make that page look foreign, and DESIGN.md currently mandates system-ui. The question is only whether to record an app-wide typeface decision as future debt.
What: Evaluate one chosen body/UI typeface app-wide and update DESIGN.md. Why: give the product a typographic voice instead of the OS default. Pros: stronger brand presence on every screen. Cons: app-wide change, font loading cost, DESIGN.md revision, visual regression across all pages. Context: flagged in Pass 4 of this review; explicitly out of scope for this form update. Depends on: /design-consultation and a DESIGN.md revision. TODOS.md does not exist yet and cannot be created in plan mode, so option A records the item in this plan and writes TODOS.md after plan mode exits.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Either the debt is forgotten, or time goes into an app-wide font change nobody asked for.
Recommendation: A because it costs nothing now and keeps an explicit design decision from being lost, while B is a fully defensible choice for a native-feeling settings surface.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: record the debt vs. accept system-ui as intentional vs. widen this PR.

options.label: A: Add to TODOS.md (recommended)
options.description:
✅ The typeface question becomes an explicit, findable decision with its context preserved
✅ Zero work in this PR; the settings form ships unchanged
❌ Creates a TODOS.md file after plan mode exits; another item to triage later

options.label: B: Skip, system-ui is intentional for this app
options.description:
✅ Native OS type is a legitimate choice for an OPERATE surface; nothing to track
✅ No new files, no future triage
❌ The decision stays implicit; a future reviewer will raise it again

options.label: C: Choose a typeface in this PR
options.description:
✅ Resolves the slop flag now rather than later
✅ The settings form ships with the final type voice
❌ Contradicts the plan's explicit no-visual-exploration constraint and touches every page (human: ~2 days / CC: ~1h)
